R-2.reason:
Not refuted. The reproduction is sound and the behaviour violates the design.

Rerun: `AGENTHUB_ROOT=/home/user/agenthub node docs/build/review/repros/R-2/protected-rename.mjs` exits 1. Output is in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agenthub/8b8b52f8-98ca-5efe-ba8a-d267c5f2c650/scratchpad/work-p23/review/refute-R-2/run.out:
- L-2 is admitted with files=["db/legacy.sql"], protected=[] and approval=[].
- The attempt ends `landed` with approvals=[].
- `git diff --name-status T0 T1` shows `M migrations/0002.sql`, and that file now contains "drop table users;".

The dist was rebuilt during my run (pipeline.js is dated 08:52:26). It still matches the source: `mergedRequirements(ctx.git, land.protected, paths, ...)` at dist pipeline.js:333/474 and src pipeline.ts:369/512. `paths` there is `protectedPaths(diffNames(base, H))`, and diffNames uses `--no-renames` (gitops queries.ts:71). gitops merge.ts recognises `CONFLICT (rename...)` messages and sets no `--no-renames`, so merge-tree's default rename detection is on. It carries the agent's edit into the protected file, and nothing computes a requirement for that file.

What the rig bypasses doesn't touch the defect: `hub.land` is called in-process instead of over HTTP, and the approval call skips the approver-token check. The approval only covers sam's rename, which was meant to be approved. Everything that produces the defect (admission, merge, requirements, the hub's `pushing` gate, the CAS push past the update hook) is the real built code. The reviewer's fixed-root control, which adds protectedPaths(diffNames(T0, C)) at P6, flips the verdict to needs_approval.

No design section allows this:
- §0.3 #14 chooses "Both": the agent's change at admission, then the merged content at the attempt (AX's option there was "candidate vs trunk").
- §4.1 #13 says requirements cover "the agent's change, the merged content", so a protected change can't land without approval.
- §1.4 and P6 define `merged` as protected paths with blob(C:p) ≠ blob(H:p). For migrations/0002.sql, C has the edited blob and H has none, so the test is met. The code never checks it because it only looks at the agent's own paths.

The input is reachable. It is plain git behaviour: trunk renames a file into a protected directory while an agent edits the old path from an older base. The same agent could also do both steps itself, and its own claims don't block it.

R-1.reason:
Not refuted. I found no design section that allows this, no evidence that real callers can't reach it, and no flaw in the reproduction that changes what it shows. I did not rerun repro.mjs. I confirmed the mechanism by reading the source instead, alongside the recorded result in /home/user/agenthub/docs/build/review/repro-results.json.

1. A real caller reaches the code. packages/lander/src/cli.ts:96 builds ChecksRunner from the lander config. packages/lander/src/pipeline.ts:378-387 calls checks.run() on every attempt with land.allowDirtyTree, which is false by default. Whenever a check exits 0, packages/lander/src/checks.ts:456 calls dirty(wt).

2. dirty() can read config the check planted. It calls open(wt,{isolated:true}). Because wt/.git exists, bare is false (packages/gitops/src/run.ts:44-46), so globalArgs() passes no --git-dir or --work-tree (run.ts:84-89). With cwd=wt, git finds the repository through whatever wt/.git is when the check ends. ISOLATION_CONFIG sets only core.hooksPath, gc.auto and merge.conflictStyle, so the repository's own core.fsmonitor is still read. childEnv() passes process.env minus GIT_* (run.ts:101-113), so a command it starts gets the lander's environment, not the allowlisted check environment.

3. The repro is sound even though it uses checkWrapper:null. dirty() runs in the lander process after the check, whatever the wrapper. The design's own wrapper example (`docker run --rm -v {wt}:/w ...`, design line 263) mounts wt read-write, so a check inside the container can replace wt/.git and the change stays on the host. HUB_LANDER_TOKEN only marks that the command ran with the lander's environment: checkEnvironment never gives HUB_* to a check. Under a real lander, SSH_AUTH_SOCK, the mirror's credential helper and lander.json are equally in reach of a command running as the lander user.

4. The design does not allow this outcome. §2.2.8 spells the check as `git -C wt status`, but it also says a check that rewrote tracked files must end as checks_modified_tree. §2.2.2's template pins --git-dir and says "no client hooks run, including in check worktrees", which is the same class of command run from config. §4.1 #11 lists checkWrapper as the prevention against stealing credentials, with a residual only "without isolation". This finding breaks that prevention under the recommended setup, which risks I1.

5. Two things narrow the finding without refuting it.
   - git's safe.directory check fails closed (dirty() returns true) when the planted .git is owned by a different uid than the lander. But a root container with Docker's default CAP_CHOWN can chown it to match /w, and nothing is needed when the container runs as the lander's uid or the lander runs as root, as here.
   - Part (B), a rewritten tree reported as passed, matters little alone: a hostile check could just exit 0, and the push sends C by sha (§4.1 #3). Part (A), a command running outside checkWrapper with the lander's credentials in reach, is enough to keep the finding blocking.

Node exited with code 1 on an uncaught ERR_STRING_TOO_LONG ('Cannot create a string longer than 0x1fffffe8 characters'), thrown at result() in run.js:149 from the ChildProcess 'close' listener (maybeClose). The try/catch around g.run did not catch it, and the lines after the call never printed. (2) The code matches the claim. In packages/gitops/src/run.ts, spawnGit calls `Buffer.concat(out).toString('utf8')` inside result(), which the 'close' listener calls before done() can reject, so no caller can catch the error. showBlob (queries.ts:85-89) returns the whole `cat-file blob` stdout. (3) A real caller reaches it. admitOne (admission.ts:133) calls admissionScope (symbols.ts:94-99), which runs showBlob(base) and showBlob(head) for every mappable changed file with no size check; its own try/catch cannot catch a throw inside the listener. No package installs an uncaughtException or unhandledRejection handler (grep of packages/*/src finds none). A submitted landing leaves that state only through the lander's own advance(to failed, attempt 0) (hub landings.ts:801). I found no deadline or attempt limit that would fail it after repeated crashes, so the crash loop on restart stands. (4) No design section allows this. §4.5 requires 'Disk full, git crash, a lander bug' to become failed {lander_error}, not a dead lander. The 'Lander crashes' row (§2.2.7 requeue) covers crashes in general, not a deterministic crash on hostile input that blocks the queue. §2.4 says oversized files map whole-file, so a size check should come before the blob is read. Caveat: my check stopped at the uncaught crash in the gitops call plus the code trace of admission. I did not run a full hub plus `hub-lander run --once` restart loop.

R-5.reason:
Not refuted. I reran the reproducer's Part A against phase23 dist with AGENTHUB_ROOT=/home/user/agenthub and REPRO_SKIP_LANDER=1 REPRO_SKIP_HOOK=1. Temp files went under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-agenthub/8b8b52f8-98ca-5efe-ba8a-d267c5f2c650/scratchpad/work-p23/review/refute-R-5/tmp. It exited 1. All six paths are quadratic: doubling n multiplies the time by 3.1 to 4.5, while each linear control stays flat.
- A1, same-line comments (changedSymbols): 1719 ms -> 5375 ms. Control: 60 ms.
- A2, Java enum constant bodies: 696 ms -> 2671 ms. Control: 10 ms.
- A3a, TS declarators: 631 ms -> 2849 ms. Control: 76 ms.
- A3b, Go typed const group: 422 ms -> 1769 ms. Control: 66 ms.
- A3c, Java field declarators: 753 ms -> 3235 ms. Control: 78 ms.
- A4, contained errors: 1282 ms -> 4048 ms. Control: 940 ms.

The code matches path (1). In packages/symbols/src/outline.ts:258, scanScope calls leadsNext for each comment on the previous element's line. leadsNext (outline.ts:477-483) then loops over every following sibling and skips comments, so a line of n comments costs O(n^2).

The reproduction is sound. It uses the built packages/*/dist and the real hub-lander bin, and it generates its temp dirs with os.tmpdir(), so it has no hardcoded scratch paths.

The design does not allow this:
- Section 2.4 maps every enabled-language file up to 1 MiB. Only files over 1 MiB fall back to too_large, and every test input is well below that (37-888 KiB).
- Section 2.4 sets budgets of under 150 ms cold for a 2000-line file and under 20 ms warm. "Logged, not gating in CI" only means CI doesn't enforce them. It does not permit multi-second-to-minute synchronous stalls.
- The guard row says "within a 10 s budget; beyond that, file-level", but one file alone can exceed 10 s because the budget is checked only between files.
- The lander lease has a 60 s TTL (section 2.2.3). Extrapolating the measured A1 curve to the Part B file (29659 comments) gives about 74 s of blocked event loop. That is consistent with the logged lease loss and with the lander_lost requeue of a bystander landing.

Two minor caveats, neither of which changes the verdict:
- I did not rerun Parts B and C because of the time limit. The Part A rerun plus the code trace establish the core defect.
- The run-default.log that the evidence cites is not present in docs/build/review/repros/R-5/.

I agree with the reproducer's correction: the queue is not permanently wedged, because the same lander process re-admits the landing from its cache. Severity stays blocking.
